# AI's $2 Trillion IPO Has a $150 Billion Question

By Beth Canova On October 13, 202612:45 PM Eastern

My Lists

AI valuations)Anthropic)artificial intelligence)investment risk)

AI's $2 Trillion IPO Has a $150 Billion Question

|
|  |
| By Beth Canova |

Imagine buying a stock for $100 … only to find out afterwards that Wall Street’s brightest think it’s only worth $7.

That's the kind of gap now facing one of the biggest IPOs of the year. [...] That growth has made AI firms some of the hottest names on Wall Street.

And it created the first notch in the gap of Anthropic’s valuation.

In May, the firm raised new funds at a value of $965 billion. Now, as it nears its initial public offering (IPO), its listing valuation has been recorded at $2 trillion.

That’s a big figure. And it’s raised some big questions. Many from our own team (but more on that in a bit).

But the most recent claims that Anthropic may be overvalued by roughly 93%. [...] AI is growing at a pace few could have seen just a few years ago.

More firms use it each day. And more people now rely on tools like ChatGPT and Claude to work, learn and save time.

To put real numbers to the trend, Statista claims the global AI market is expected to hit an incredible valuation near $707.48 billion by the end of this year.

And it expects the market to grow at a steady annual growth rate 18.52% through 2032.

The central question is not whether artificial intelligence is real or commercially valuable. It clearly is. The question is whether IPOs are becoming the mechanism through which extraordinary private valuations, persistent operating losses and increasingly leveraged infrastructure commitments are transferred from venture investors to public-market balance sheets. [...] That creates a second risk channel beyond IPO valuations: leverage turns an equity repricing into a credit event.

Much of the broader venture cohort has undergone a painful reset from 2021 marks, while leading AI companies have moved in the opposite direction. That creates an unusual exit environment: public investors may be asked to absorb businesses at valuations dramatically above previous private rounds even while profitability remains uncertain. news.title: 风投人士：Goldman和JPMorgan正成为AI概念股
news.snippet: Qu表示，银行通过为AI基础设施建设提供债务融资涉足AI，传统投行正被视作AI股票投资标的。
news.raw_snippet:
Qu said banks now touch AI through debt financing for the buildout. They also take part in potential initial public offerings (IPOs) and mergers.

She expects banks to sit at the center of more mergers as that activity rises.

However, lending profit was a highlight of the quarter. JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo posted a record $56.5 billion in combined net interest income, Bloomberg reported. [...] Qu said investors split into two camps on AI valuations.

One camp gives AI firms a pass on margins and capital spending because revenue is growing so fast.

In contrast, the other camp expects public markets to demand higher margins and proof that spending pays off.

Anthropic holds its pre-IPO investor day on Wednesday. Qu expects speculation over which camp prevails until the company lists.

She said other AI companies may wait to list until they see how markets price the leaders. [...] Separately, billionaire Paul Tudor Jones warned that a flood of AI listings could make 2027 difficult for US stocks.

Banks that fund and underwrite those listings could therefore share in any repricing of AI valuations.
